basis: The printing heads this block 'VERS. 12.' and it opens 'VERS. 12.-- Et indicavit ei quod frater esset patris ejus et filius Rebeccae. Bene ait,'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Angelomus was a monk of Luxeuil in the middle of the ninth century and wrote for the Emperor Lothar I, who reigned from 840 to 855 and whom the verse prooemium addresses. The Genesis commentary is placed with his commentaries on Kings and on the Song of Songs in that decade. The wiki header gives the eleventh century, which is a century and a half out and is not followed. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1852 printing.
text: VERS. 12.-- Et indicavit ei quod frater esset patris ejus et filius Rebeccae. Bene ait, et indicavit quod frater esset patris ejus et filius Rebeccae. Quia ex stirpe patriarcharum et ex Synagoga Judaeorum Dominus incarnari dignatus est: At illa festinans nuntiavit patri suo. Quia Ecclesia non exstitit contenta solummodo propria salute, sed gentibus atque sapientibus hujus mundi praedicare studuit.
